data.narrative:
Xage Security is a Series B-stage defense and security company that has raised $80M to date. The valuation analysis relies on a comparables universe of 8 private peers and 2 public companies operating in the Defense & Security sector at similar stages.

Two triangulation methods are applied here. Stage-progression analysis uses total raised as a proxy valuation base, applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $152M. Peer-median analysis draws on 8 same-sector, same-stage private companies—including Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B)—which establish a median valuation of $1.1B against a range of $300M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis produces a low of $129M, median of $638M, and high of $1.3B. The wide spread reflects material dispersion within the peer set: stage-progression implies conservative pricing relative to median comparables, suggesting either that Xage commands a discount to sector peers or that peer valuations embed late-stage financing premiums. Key uncertainties include revenue scale and growth trajectory relative to named peers, and whether public comps (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) anchor expectations differently than private precedent.
